profile.headline: Embedded Software Engineer @ Astrolab
profile.summary:
As an Embedded Software Engineer at Axiom Space, I support the development of the world's first commercial space station, a groundbreaking project that will revolutionize the space industry and human exploration. I am the responsible engineer for the software of the Telemetry Tracking and command (TT&C) communication system, which is essential for the safe and reliable operation of the Axiom Visiting Vehicle during Rendezvous Proximity Operations and Capture (RPOC).

I have a strong background in electrical engineering, with a Master of Science degree from Texas A&M University, where I worked on research and development projects involving instrumentation, embedded systems, PCBA, control systems, Python, C/C++, signal processing, and analog & digital circuit design. Some of my past professional highlights include designing and modeling the electronics for the ARGOS 3 (AX3S) human-in-loop simulation system at NASA, and developing a control system to enable human torso imaging via Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) at 7 Tesla at the Magnetic Resonance Systems Lab at TEES. I am driven by curiosity, innovation, and challenge, and I enjoy working on cutting-edge technologies that have the potential to make a positive impact on humanity and the world.

· Lead/mentored an integrated of 10 embedded flight software engineers for Communications, GN&C, Propulsion, State Machine, FDIR, Power and ECLSS subsystems

· Manage and allocate resources (people, time, budget, tools) for maximum results for both the product, team members, and program milestones
· Ensure Risk (Technical, Financial, Schedule, blockers) are solved, mitigated, and/or tracked
· Determine Milestones for cross team development, integration, and testing

positions.title: Embedded Software Engineer
positions.description:
I support the development of world's first Commerical Space Station

· Designed and Architectured various aspects of the flight software 
· Responsible Engineer over all software for Telemetry Tracking & Command (TT&C) communication system to be used on the Axiom module during Rendezvous Proximity Operations, and Capture (RPOC)
· Worked across the software development lifecycle for the Flight Control systems
· Designed the system to have two independent strings operation with the ability for both strings to fail-safe modes.
· Accelerated software development of the team by automating and simplifying the build systems and CI/CD pipelines 
· Built HWIL Testbed for rapid prototyping/testing of hardware/software of the communications system
· Implemented framework and infrastructure software to distribution multiple applications/firmware
· Wrote & Reviewed, Refined requirements for the communication system
· Integrated Communication Systems with other systems on the vehicle such command and data handling, GNC, Ground systems
· Wrote application and embedded Flight Software and test software for radios, microcontrollers (Antenna Router Board for Transmit/ Active Receive Antennas), and Crypto Modules
· Designed RF PCB for Flight including simulation, schematics, and layout.

company.name: NASA - National Aeronautics and Space Administration

positions.title: Space Robotics Electrical Systems Hardware Engineer
positions.description:
ARGOS, ER5, JSC
• ARGOS 3 also known as AX3S(ARGOS eXploration EVA Simulator) is a Human in Loop simulation used to perform multiple participant gravity offload
• Worked as the Electrical System Architect in designing/usage/placement of all Electronics, Cables, EtherCAT modules, Network infrastructure, and the system as a whole
• Modeled in Altium all of electronics for various subsystems such as the Control System, Power, Network infrastructure, Audio/Video, and cables/Wiring Harness
• Evaluated the system to make sure the stakeholder’s requirements and desires were met or had ability to be met given additional resources in the future
• Architectured the Computing Network to be resilient to outside attack but also functional for use by developers, operator, and customers
• Performed tasks such as planning of current goals, induvial objectives of the team members, Coordinating with Mechanical/Software teams, research and documentation
• Designed electrical power/signal cables/wiring harness to be used throughout the ARGOS 3 Control/ Power/Network Systems
• Streamlined tracking of parts to determine which parts were the most critical for development and order

positions.title: Space Systems Avionics Integration Engineer
positions.description:
Orion Test Labs, ER7, JSC
•Wrote software to communicate with PXI, PCI, and USB ADIO/Serial hardware from NI, NAI, and Pickering
•Aided in the setup and management of the lab servers and ADIO pumps
•Setup Gitlab CI/CD for automated testing of multiple software products
•Streamlined software used in the wrap test(automated Orion cable testing of over 5000 Electrical Connections) in ITL(Integrated Test Lab) to debug the Orion database and automating operation
•Supported integration and development of the Systems Engineering Simulator(SES) beta dome hardware with OrionSim simulating the vehicle performance and human in the loop testing
•Expanded OrionSim Interface’s (Orion CrewStation Application) capability to communicate between OrionSim and COTS/GOTS hardware via ethernet additionality allows rapidly interchanging hardware
•Designed and Prototyped cockpit Hardware Interface using an Arduino Due to communicate over a TCP/IP Socket
•Analyzed Orion software products from Lockheed Martin(LM) for functionality, and performance
•Improved upon Integrated Orion and Gateway simulation for HIL docking capabilities exercising FSW and telemetry
Virtual Reality Lab, ER7, JSC
•Aided in the upgrade of the SAFER Virtual Reality (VR) Trick Simulation Software from RHEL4 to RHEL7 
•Integrated the trick-simulation with new NI PCIe hardware performing real-time Human/Hardware in the Loop 
•Evaluated potential ADIO boards to determine if timing, durability, power, and other design requirements are met

positions.title: Space Robotics Electrical Systems Hardware Engineer
positions.description: Contractor to NASA Johnson Space Center

positions.title: Researcher at Magnetic Resonance Systems Lab
positions.description:
•Invented novel approach to perform dynamic B1+ Steering for human torso magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to study cancer detection at 7 Tesla resulting in savings of $2 million
•Built control system for body coil to manipulate transmit phase on 8 channel array to focus B1 field by performing B1+ Steering at 298MHz
•Designed, simulated, and assembled PCBs using PSpice and Kicad for RF, glue logic, noise suppression, and amplifiers to correctly adapt developed system to 7 Tesla MRI scanner at University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center
•Integrated system composed of a microcontroller, single board computer, fiber optic communication, and host computer utilizing Python to operate correctly near strong magnetic fields and prevent image distortion
•Established protocols to determine accuracy of data acquired and system's operation to implement feedback system
•Trained/Lead 7 graduate and undergraduate students in operating lab equipment, operating an LPKF, and project management

positions.title: Lane Detection Team Lead for the GM/SAE AutoDrive Challenge, Texas A&M University
positions.description:
•Created and designed autonomous vehicle(Chevy Bolt) capable of making sharp turns, maneuvering through obstacles and detecting traffic signs or level 2 autonomy stated by SAE standards within one year of development
•Won 2nd place in AutoDrive year 1 competition representing TAMU, competing against 7 other universities
•Collaborated on interdisciplinary team of 60 students from different departments 
•Developed Image Processing algorithm using OpenCV-Python to pull desired characteristics from traffic lanes such as distance, whether lines are solid or dashed and curvature of the lane 
•Devised method to accurately stop vehicle within required distance being only team to meet goal
•Integrated subsystems with others using ROS to allocate resources and increase performance of overall system
•Coordinated between lane detection team, professors, other team leads, and management team on tasks, progress, communication within software architecture

positions.title: Hardware Engineering Intern
positions.description:
• Devised test procedure to accelerate testing of products from 2 years to be accomplished within 2 weeks in controlled and automated test environment with safe and easy access
• Created specs, designed, and built system to cycle dust and collect data to simulate Air Duct environment to study reliability and life span of products
• Designed and integrated control instruments into testing environment to implement closed loop feedback system controlled through LabVIEW to automate process for easy operation
• Utilized DAQ 6008 along with external circuity to precisely control servo & stepper motors, linear actuators, and electric air valve. Function generator and Power supplies were controlled using GPIB interface.
• Collaborated in design review and validation of products in lab before market and Underwriters Laboratories testing to ensure customer satisfaction after production of products

positions.title: Autonomous Building Lighting Assessments - AggiE_Challenge
positions.description:
• Collaborated on an interdisciplinary project with many diverse engineering majors
• Tasked with creating an autonomous, modular device that efficiently completes light audits
• Created a handheld method to maneuver the device for testing purposes and visually show the placement of lights on a 2.5D rendered map

positions.title: Tutor

• Kept attendance of current students in classes
• Graded homework and classwork for students

organizations.name: First Robotics Competition
organizations.description:
•	Improved understanding of engineering background working with mechanical, electrical, civil and programming engineers on building a robot in less than 6 weeks
•	Designed and Built with real-life engineering constraints and similar work-like environment with in a team of 30 students 		
•	Coordinated team safety, with all power tools, equipment, and hardware
•	Repaired and made adjustments to the robot under a small amount of time for unpredictable occurrences
•	Represented team to judges, scouters, viewers, and safety inspectors on history of the team, team performance and reasons why our team could be a asset to others 
•	Nominated by mentors/teachers and voted on by peers
